title: Complete, stably ordered paginated retrieval from the VCF Operations API
prompt:
Fix the symptom-definition retrieval in opsclient/client.go. The package is a dependency-free Go client for the VMware Cloud Foundation Operations 9.1 API and uses three operations: acquireToken (POST /api/auth/token/acquire), getSymptomDefinitions (GET /api/symptomdefinitions), and releaseToken (POST /api/auth/token/release). Its transport, error handling and response decoding already work, but ListSymptomDefinitions returns whatever the first page happened to contain, in whatever order the appliance sent it, and it builds requests that assert filters the caller never asked for.

ListSymptomDefinitions must return the whole collection the filter selects, no matter how many pages the appliance splits it across. Pagination is by page number starting at 0; page-info.totalCount reports the total number of results and is what decides that the collection is complete, so the client must stop once it has collected that many entries rather than requesting a further page to discover it is empty. The merged result must be emitted in a stable order: ascending by symptom-definition id, byte-wise, regardless of the order pages or entries arrived in. Every optional field the caller left unset must be absent from the request rather than sent empty: adapterKind, resourceKind, name and id must not appear in the query string at all when unset, and the optional authSource property must not be sent as an empty string or as null. `page` and `pageSize` are always sent, with `pageSize` defaulting to 1000. Values of the repeated id parameter keep the caller's order. The client is documented as safe for concurrent use once a token has been acquired, so overlapping retrievals on one client must not race or share result storage; each caller gets its own slice.

Add `ReleaseToken(ctx context.Context) error`. It must send the current token in the `Authorization` header, send no body or `Content-Type`, clear the stored token only after a successful release, and make repeated calls with no stored token succeed without network traffic.\n\nBefore implementing, research the VCF Operations `acquireToken`, `getSymptomDefinitions`, and `releaseToken` operations in official VMware sources. Cite the sources consulted in the final answer. Preserve the existing exported API of the package and add only the `ReleaseToken` method described above. Run `go test -race ./verifier/...` to check your work. Edit only `opsclient/client.go`.
